Operator:
    Good morning, and welcome to the Global Aerospace Corporation Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up can be found by pressing * followed by 1 on your telephone keypad. Please note this event is being recorded.

    I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
    Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Aerospace Corporation's Q3 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Strategy Officer; Amanda Torres, Chief Marketing Officer; and David Patel, Chief Compliance Officer.

    Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those statements.

Johnathan Hale:
    Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Global Aerospace Corporation delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across defense, space, commercial aviation, and services. We reported revenue of $8.7 billion, up 9% year-over-year, with segment-adjusted EBIT margins expanding to 13.2%. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders.

    Today, we'll cover our strategic priorities and outlook, commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery, gross margin and operating margin analysis along with net income, drivers of aftermarket performance, free cash flow generation and utilization, capital deployment strategy, revenue breakdown by segment, and the expansion of our service offerings and customer base. We're particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NGAD program and its potential to establish leadership in sixth-generation air dominance technologies. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, including F-35 sustainment and hypersonic prototypes, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily with stabilizing production lines.

    With that overview, I'll turn it over to Michael for a deeper dive into our financial results and key aspects.

Michael Rivera:
    Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. Let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $8.7 billion, representing a 9% increase year-over-year, driven by a record $125 billion funded backlog with a book-to-bill of 1.15x and $4.2 billion in new program awards this quarter. Our diluted earnings per share were $2.85, up 22% from last year. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $15 billion in cash and equivalents and robust liquidity. Our guidance for the full year remains unchanged at revenue of $38.5 to $40.0 billion, segment-adjusted EBIT of $5.1 to $5.4 billion, and free cash flow of $3.8 to $4.2 billion. We are actively managing our costs through initiatives like GLEAN and investing in key growth areas while returning capital to shareholders.

    Our specific financial highlights include gross margin of 19.2%, operating income reflecting 13.4% margins, and free cash flow of $1.25 billion for the quarter.

    Starting with our strategic priorities and outlook for Q4 and full-year 2025, our focus remains on three pillars: accelerating next-generation capabilities in contested environments, fortifying supply chain resilience amid geopolitical volatility, and capitalizing on the commercial aviation rebound while advancing sustainable technologies. In Defense Systems, our growth engine at 52% of revenue with $4.5 billion in Q3 up 12% year-over-year, we're scaling sixth-generation air dominance under NGAD. We've allocated an additional $450 million in FY25 CapEx for digital engineering fly-by-wire systems and AI-enabled collaborative combat aircraft drones, with early test flights achieving Mach 0.9 and 98% mission reliability, ahead of competitors. U.S. DoD spending anchors us with the FY25 NDAA's 4.5% increase to $895 billion, including $28 billion for hypersonics where we hold 22% market share. In the Indo-Pacific, tensions have boosted our pipeline 15% with a $1.2 billion IDIQ from Japan for Patriot GEM-T and hypersonic defenses. Europe accelerates post-Ukraine with NATO's 2% GDP pledge yielding €650 million in F-35 wing production for Poland and Romania, while the Middle East sees $800 million backlog from Saudi THAAD systems. We guide Q4 Defense revenue to $4.8 to $4.9 billion, FY25 at $19.0 to $19.5 billion with margins at 14.0 to 14.5%.

    In Space & Missile Defense, 28% of revenue at $2.4 billion up 14%, we're prioritizing proliferated low-Earth orbit constellations for resilient comms and ISR, investing $600 million to scale our 150-satellite HawkEye network with 30% lower SWaP via photonic payloads, aligning with Space Force's $30 billion request. U.S. commercial space booms with New Glenn-class launches, AUKUS opens $5 billion opportunities, and India's Chandrayaan-4 adds $400 million. Q4 guidance: $2.6 to $2.7 billion, FY25 $10.5 to $11.0 billion at 15.5 to 16.0% margins.

    Commercial Aviation, 20% of revenue at $1.8 billion up 5%, focuses on sustainable tech like hybrid-electric propulsion for NASA's X-66A targeting 30% fuel burn reduction and 100% SAF compatibility on LEAP-X blades for the $1.2 trillion MRO market. North America drives 60% orders, Asia-Pacific surges 20% on Air India's 470-plane deal, Europe gaps filled by aftermarket. Q4: $1.9 to $2.0 billion, FY25 $8.0 to $8.5 billion at 10.5 to 11.0% margins.

    Overarching enablers include derisking 85% of titanium and rare earths via reshoring, with CASM up just 2% despite 7% inflation, plus 5,000 new engineers and $200 million in PLM software cutting NGAD cycles 25%. Q4 consolidated revenue $9.3 to $9.6 billion. Upside from $15 billion international pipeline; risks like DoD CR delays mitigated by buffers, commercial slips. With global budgets at $2.4 trillion up 6.8%, we're executing flawlessly, fueled by $1.1 billion IRA/CHIPS credits for 18%+ ROIC.

    On commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery trajectory, pre-pandemic we hit 580 units annually across AGD-700 narrowbodies and AGD-900 widebodies, 15% share. COVID slashed to 210 in 2020; now Q3 saw 142 deliveries, up 28% YoY and 18% sequentially, 75% of 2019 pace with narrowbodies at 95 units (67% recovery) and widebodies 47 (55%). YTD 262 on track for 550-575 full-year, backlog $482 billion or 8.2 years, 62% post-2022 orders. Trends: RPKs up 12%, 15% orders for AGD-700X with 20% better SFC. Asia-Pacific 64 units up 35% with IndiGo/Air India, 25% localization in Chengdu. North America 35 units, Europe 22 up 15%, Middle East/LATAM 15 widebodies. Factory 4.0 boosts AGD-700 to 42/month targeting 50, $1.2 billion in additive for 15% weight savings, 70% tier-1 diversification. Defense composites flow in, SAF by 2028. Challenges: GTF inspections, titanium risks; $15 billion cash for $3 billion CapEx. Full recovery to 600+ by mid-2026.

    Drilling into gross margin, operating margin, and net income: Gross margins at 19.2%, up 140 bps YoY and 50 bps sequentially, strongest in three years from mix shift to high-margin fixed-price, $250 million YTD savings from digital twins on NGAD reducing scrap 22% and ECOs 15%, additive cutting COGS 18%. Pricing discipline added 60 bps, Defense at 21.5%, Space 18.0%, Commercial 14.2%. U.S. gov sales drove 200 bps, Europe +10%. Offset $45 million titanium charge. Operating margins 13.4%, up 110 bps, SG&A 4.2% down from 4.8%, R&D $420 million capitalized 2.1%. $120 million divestiture gain, segment ops Defense 15.2%, Space 12.8%, Commercial 9.5%. Net income $920 million or $2.85 EPS up 22%, tax 21.5% with FDII, interest $65 million offset by JV income. FCF $1.1 billion supports repurchases and dividend hike. Targeting FY gross 19.0%, ops 13.2%; structurally improving to 5th/6th-gen.

    Aftermarket performance drivers: Revenues $2.8 billion up 18%, 42% of top line, EBITDA 31.2% up 220 bps. Fleet utilization at 88% commercial (96% traffic), 97% defense with F135 1.2 million hours up 14%, V-22 up 30%. Maintenance cycles: 185 shop visits/1,000 engines up, GTF early shops, F110 1,800-hour cadence. Digital Twin 92% accuracy cuts removals 17%, additive 40% lead times. North America 55%, Europe 24%, APAC 32%, Middle East 22%. Installed base 28,000 up 4%, $45 billion backlog, TrueChoice 65% new engines. Guide 16-18% growth, 30%+ margins.

    Free cash flow generation: $1.25 billion up 39%, TTM $4.8 billion on track $4.9-$5.3 billion. Op cash $2.1 billion up 28%, Defense $1.6 billion from F-35 Block 4, commercial $450 million. DSO 52 days, conversion 115%. CapEx $850 million or 4.2%. Utilization: 40% dividends $500 million hike to $0.48, 30% buybacks $375 million 1.2% shares, 20% debt reduction to 1.8x leverage, 10% M&A. Tailwinds: $61 billion aid unlocks $2.5 billion IDIQs, AUKUS $800 million. 'Cash Fortress' for $500 million WC frees, SDA $200 million.

    Revenue by segment: Total $26.4 billion up 12%. Commercial Aerospace $11.2 billion (42%) up 28% on 185 narrowbodies, backlog $450 billion 1.4x, North America 55%, Europe 25%, APAC 18%. Defense $12.1 billion (46%) up 6% on F-35 Lot 15 $2.8 billion, hypersonics $1.2 billion, backlog $380 billion 12.5% margins. Services $3.1 billion (12%) up 18% on MRO $1.1 billion LEAP, freighters $600 million, APAC 25%, Europe 16%. Q4 for $105 billion full-year up 14%.

    Expansion of service offerings and customer base: Services $4.2 billion up 28%, 32% mix, EBITA 18.2%. AeroPredict reduces events 22%, $1.8 billion Navy IDIQ, $750 million LRHW, SDA-as-a-Service. Customers to 142 up 32%, $3.4 billion new backlog total $52.7 billion. Indo-Pacific 35% growth AUKUS/Japan, Middle East 42% C4ISR, Europe 25% Tempest, commercial Delta/Emirates. Targeting 40% mix by 2026, 20%+ ROIC.

    Capital deployment strategy remains balanced for superior TSR: 40% dividends with 17th hike, 30% opportunistic repurchases like $1.5 billion this year, debt reduction, tuck-ins amid long-cycle tailwinds.

Lisa Chen:
    Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in supply chain management, derisking 85% of critical materials through U.S. and allied reshoring, limiting CASM to 2% rise. We've increased production rates on key programs like F-35 and NGAD, investing in automation, digital twins, and AI-optimized assembly to cut build times 18% and boost line rates to 42 per month on commercial platforms, targeting 50 by year-end. Labor additions of 4,200 with 3.2% attrition, plus Industry 4.0 factories yielding 95% on-time deliveries.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
    Thank you, Lisa. On the technology front, we're advancing next-generation propulsion with hybrid-electric for X-66A at 30% fuel savings, LEAP-X SAF compatibility, and hypersonic prototypes hitting Mach 0.9. Digital twins and additive manufacturing reduce scrap 22%, lead times 40%, giving us edge in NGAD CCA drones, GPI interceptors, and pLEO HawkEye with photonic payloads.

Robert Kline:
    Thank you, Elena. Strategically, we're evaluating acquisitions to complement our portfolio, like MRO bolt-ons, expanding into SDA and hypersonics services. New models capture AUKUS, NATO opportunities, leveraging $52.7 billion backlog for 1.4x book-to-bill in services.

Amanda Torres:
    Thank you, Robert. Marketing efforts highlight our branding around resilient defense and sustainable commercial tech, resonating via digital channels. Success in APAC with Air India visibility, North America fleet modernizations, driving 32% customer growth and 28% services surge.

Operator:
    Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Instructions as before. Our first question comes from Alex Thompson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Alex Thompson:
    Good morning. Can you provide more color on the commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery trajectory, especially Asia-Pacific ramp?

Johnathan Hale:
    Certainly, Alex. As Michael detailed, Q3 deliveries hit 142 up 28% YoY, on pace for 550-575 full-year at 95% of 2019 narrowbody levels. Asia-Pacific led with 64 units, 35% growth from IndiGo and Air India's massive order ramping H2 2025, our Chengdu JV securing 15% share gain despite COMAC. Factory 4.0 and supplier diversification position us for 600+ by mid-2026.

Operator:
    Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
    Hi, thanks. Curious about gross margin expansion drivers and sustainability into FY25?

Michael Rivera:
    Maria, margins expanded 140 bps to 19.2% from digital transformation savings of $250 million YTD, additive on hypersonics cutting COGS 18%, and favorable mix in Defense at 21.5%. Pricing on CPFF added 60 bps, OpEx leverage with SG&A down to 4.2%. Sustainable via exiting low-margin commercial, pivoting to F-35 sustainment and NGAD LRIP, targeting another 100 bps in FY25 with international backlog insulating risks.

Operator:
    Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
    Regarding the drivers of aftermarket performance, how are fleet utilization and maintenance cycles trending into Q4?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
    David, utilization at 88% commercial and 97% defense, with F135 logging 1.2 million hours up 14% from ops in Middle East/Europe. Cycles compressing: 185 commercial shop visits/1,000 engines, F110 to 1,800 hours. Our Digital Twin at 92% accuracy extends time-on-wing 250 hours, additive cuts parts leads 40%, supporting 16-18% growth guide with 30%+ margins.

Operator:
    Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
    Question about free cash flow utilization and potential for more share repurchases?

Michael Rivera:
    Emily, Q3 FCF $1.25 billion up 39%, deployed 40% to dividends hiked to $0.48, 30% buybacks retiring 1.2% shares opportunistically. Leverage at 1.8x gives flexibility; with $4.9-$5.3 billion full-year, we'll continue balanced approach including tuck-ins, prioritizing TSR as budgets swell to $850 billion FY25.

Johnathan Hale:
    Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation across defense, space, and commercial sectors.

Sarah Jenkins:
    Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 earnings call. A replay and transcript will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
    This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
